header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Hand-transcribed; sha256 is of the canonical body. Marked 'projected' ONLY because the 2026 inflation-indexed 65+ subtraction has not been published (2026 Form 2 instructions not yet released); the 2025 amount ($5,660) is used. Rates and brackets are enacted law, per the Department of Revenue's HB 337 notice (2025-11-14): 4.7% on taxable income up to $47,500 (single/MFS), $71,250 (HOH), $95,000 (MFJ); 5.65% above (2027: 4.7% to $65,000/$97,500/$130,000 and 5.4% above). Montana starts from FEDERAL TAXABLE INCOME, so the federal standard deduction (2026: $16,100 single / $32,200 MFJ) or itemized deductions are already embedded: standardDeduction and personalExemption are 0 here. Note the federal OBBBA senior deduction and other federal deductions flow through to the extent Montana conforms. Net long-term capital gains (and qualified dividends) are taxed separately at lower rates: 3.0% on gains that fall below the ordinary-bracket threshold ($47,500/$71,250/$95,000) after stacking on ordinary income, 4.1% above; the brackets above apply to taxable income excluding net long-term gains. Roughly equivalent to a 27%-36% exclusion relative to the ordinary rates. Social Security is taxed to the same extent as federally (included in federal taxable income; no state exemption). No general pension/IRA exclusion since 2024; taxpayers 65+ subtract $5,660 each (2025 amount, indexed); a partial military-retirement subtraction exists for some working retirees. Montana EITC is 20% of the federal credit from 2026.
